product.reading: Reading the spans of the last hour.

attention.storageDetail: VictoriaTraces, which keeps the spans inside this container, does not answer. Spans sent now are refused, and the screens are empty until it does; Traces starts it again on its own. Its logs are in the container's.
attention.disk: Only {{free}} free on the data volume
attention.diskDetail: When the volume is fuller than TRACES_MAX_DISK_PERCENT, the oldest days of spans are dropped first. Give the volume more space or keep spans for fewer days (TRACES_RETENTION_DAYS).
attention.readOnly: The volume is too full: VictoriaTraces takes no spans until there is room again.

services.description: Every service that sends spans, with the rate, errors and latency of the requests it answers.
services.noneDetail: Services appear here once their OpenTelemetry SDK or collector sends spans to Traces.

service.description: {{spans}} spans and {{endpoints}} endpoints in this window
service.quietDetail: The service sent spans, but answered no requests: it only calls others or works on its own. Choose a longer window to see more.
service.latencyDetail: Of the requests it answered: p50, p95 and p99
service.latencyOf: Latency of {{name}}: p50, p95 and p99
service.endpointsDetail: Its requests by span name, slowest first
service.failed: The service could not be read

objective.title: Objective of {{name}}
objective.detail: The p95 latency and the share of failed requests it should stay under. Leave one empty to watch only the other. Above either, the service is marked on every screen.

endpoints.description: Every request of every service, by span name: for HTTP, the method and route.

traces.description: The latest traces with a span that matches every filter. Pick one to see it as a waterfall.
traces.noneDetail: Widen the window or take a filter away. A span can be found about 30 seconds after it arrives.
traces.pickOne: Pick a trace to see its waterfall.

trace.pick: Pick a span to see its attributes.

map.description: Who calls whom, from client and server spans. Pick a service to see its callers and what it calls.
map.topologyDetail: Left to right: services nothing instrumented calls, the services they call, then databases, queues and hosts that send no spans.
map.slowestDetail: The slowest call in this window, over {{calls}} calls. Open the traces of the caller to see which requests wait for it.
map.noneDetail: The map is drawn from the spans of services that call each other. Send spans, or choose a longer window.
map.noCallers: No instrumented callers: requests enter here.

compare.description: Each endpoint's latency, errors and rate in one period and in another, such as the same hour yesterday.

bases.day: The same time a day earlier
bases.week: The same time a week earlier

compare.changeDetail: How much p95 latency changed from the period it is compared with.
compare.same: No endpoint is much slower than before
compare.byEndpointDetail: Endpoints with the most requests in either period, at most 500

setupPage.description: How to send spans to Traces and read them from Grafana.
setupPage.sdkDetail: Every SDK reads these variables. Use TRACES_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.
setupPage.collectorDetail: The collector's otlphttp exporter, protobuf over HTTPS; gzip is taken.
setupPage.grafanaDetail: Traces answers Jaeger's query API at /jaeger, so Grafana takes it as a Jaeger data source with an API token of the viewer role.
setupPage.semanticsDetail: The same rules on every screen and in the API.
setupPage.ruleTrace: A trace is every span with the same trace ID.
setupPage.ruleRequest: A service's requests are its server and consumer spans, and the root spans of traces it starts. Latency and errors of services and endpoints are read from them.
setupPage.ruleError: A request failed when its span has the status ERROR.
setupPage.ruleMap: A call is a client or producer span. It goes to the service whose server or consumer span answered it, or else to the database, queue or host its attributes name.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Traces.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Traces, and with which role. Viewers see and search everything; editors also set objectives and push spans; admins also manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For Grafana, collectors, scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
